I ran one job (ID 01a16483-4f89-74ac-86fa-510113e4bf37) on IQM's free Emerald test device, emerald:mock. The job had 4 circuits with 250 shots each, and it completed. The mock costs no credits.

What I built. Each circuit uses all 54 qubits of Emerald, one qubit per atom. Every qubit starts in 0. One time step applies RX(theta) to every qubit. Then it applies RZZ(-pi/2) = exp(i pi/4 ZZ) once on each coupler. I took the coupler list from the real emerald's current calibration (calibration set 3a1a9ad0-0c98-49db-8cf5-7623d13729f4). That calibration lists 85 CZ couplers. The mock lists 90, because it still has 5 couplers that the real chip has dropped (QB6-QB7, QB15-QB23, QB24-QB32, QB49-QB50, QB50-QB54). I left those 5 out. Each RZZ became exactly one native CZ. The extra Z turns that RZZ needs went into the phase of the next single-qubit pulse, so they add no gates. I sent the native circuits as written, with no transpiler. Nothing could add, merge, or remove a coupler gate. I read the job back from the server. Each circuit has 255 CZ gates, which is 85 couplers times 3 steps. Each step uses every listed coupler exactly once. All 54 qubits, QB1 to QB54, are measured. Before I submitted, I checked on a 14-qubit patch that the native circuit gives the same probabilities as the RX plus RZZ circuit.

What a perfect quantum computer would show. I computed the noise-free magnetization of the circuits I submitted, using each qubit's exact light cone. The magnetization is the average of Z over all 54 qubits.
- theta = 0: 1.000. With no sideways field, nothing flips, and every magnet stays up.
- theta = 0.2 pi: 0.452
- theta = 0.35 pi: 0.113
- theta = 0.5 pi: 0.000

A stronger sideways field tips the spins further out of the up direction at every kick. The couplers then mix each spin with its neighbors. Within 3 steps, the order melts. At theta = 0.5 pi, a perfect machine gives exactly zero magnetization.

What the mock returned. The measured magnetizations were 0.007, 0.056, -0.044, and 0.005. All four are near zero, and the theta = 0 circuit gives about 0 instead of 1. This does not show the physics. The mock does not simulate the circuit. It checks that the job is valid and then returns random bitstrings, so its counts do not depend on the field. To see the real melting curve, run the same job on the real emerald. Noise there would pull the values toward zero, so they would probably come out below the ideal 1.0, 0.45, 0.11, 0.

The principle. A sideways field fights the magnets' up-down order. The kicked Ising model shows the fight as a field-strength dial. A weak field leaves the sheet mostly magnetized. A strong field (theta = pi/2) wipes out the average magnetization in a few steps.

Data notes. In counts_list, each bitstring puts QB1 on the left. The counts field holds the last circuit (theta = 0.5 pi).
